phases.purpose: Establish sustainable frequency, low-intensity volume, and controlled quality.
Progress volume, long-run capacity, and demanding-session duration.
Reduce planned load while retaining normal running rhythm.
Practice bounded half-marathon-specific work after the aerobic build.
Reduce accumulated fatigue while retaining frequency and small intensity doses.
Arrive at and execute the target event.

intensity_distribution.easy_effort_guidance: Conversational running, normally RPE 2-4 out of 10.
intensity_distribution.quality_effort_guidance: Controlled demanding work, normally RPE 6-8; repetitions stop before form deteriorates.

workout_categories.description: Intervals, hills, threshold, or race-specific work.

workout_recipes.description: A full day without scheduled running.
A mostly easy long run bounded by weekly distance and progression rules.
Short controlled uphill repetitions with easy downhill recovery.
Structured repetitions with recoveries and complete warm-up and cooldown.
Controlled sustained work divided into bounded segments.
One continuous controlled threshold segment with complete warm-up and cooldown.
Race-specific segments anchored to the supported pace rather than an unsupported aspirational target.
A short controlled quality segment early in race week, separated from the goal event.
Effort-based uphill repetitions with controlled downhill recovery.
Effort-based climbing or rolling trail work without a flat-road pace target.
The trail half marathon using course-aware effort and power-hiking guidance.
A time-based quality session with explicit easy support and controlled work.
A time-based mostly conversational long run or hike.

rules.summary: Support one half marathon over 55-168 days with 3-6 distance-based or 2-6 duration-based core running days.
rules.product_assumption: This is a deliberately bounded product scope; load basis, running frequency, and terrain are independent planning dimensions rather than physiological boundaries.

rules.summary: Progress from foundation through race-specific preparation to one taper and race peak.
rules.product_assumption: A transparent traditional phase sequence is preferred over concentrated high-intensity blocks for the first recreational half-marathon policy.

rules.summary: Estimate current half-marathon equivalence from the strongest recent hard performance and expose uncertainty.
rules.product_assumption: Distance-specific uncertainty bands are conservative review values and are not confidence intervals from the cited study.

rules.summary: Recommend a rounded supported target and classify faster requests without changing policy constraints.
rules.product_assumption: Projected improvement, readiness multipliers, rounding, and aspirational-gap limits are bounded product assumptions for transparent goal setting.

rules.summary: Limit planned build-week volume changes and the peak relative to the stated baseline.
rules.product_assumption: The 10 percent build cap smooths generated plans; it is not presented as a proven injury-prevention threshold.

rules.summary: Insert reduced-volume recovery weeks after two or three build weeks.
rules.product_assumption: Fixed recovery-week timing and reduction ranges are conservative defaults pending individual response data.

rules.summary: Keep 75-90 percent of planned running at low intensity and limit demanding sessions.
rules.product_assumption: The exact percentage range and two-session cap operationalize a pyramidal approach for recreational runners.

rules.summary: Bound long-run progression, weekly share, and peak distance.
rules.product_assumption: The two-kilometre increment, 40 percent share, and 21-kilometre peak are plan-construction bounds rather than proven universal injury thresholds.

rules.summary: Taper for 7-21 days by reducing volume 41-60 percent while retaining core frequency and small intensity doses.
rules.product_assumption: The generator will select a duration inside the evidence-supported range according to total plan length.

rules.summary: Separate demanding sessions with at least one easy or rest day.
rules.product_assumption: This is a conservative scheduling constraint for a general recreational plan.

rules.summary: Keep optional recovery running small and removable without compensation.
rules.product_assumption: Optional sessions must remain behaviorally optional and cannot be required to meet core volume.

rules.summary: Do not stack a missed workout later if doing so compromises demanding-session spacing.
rules.product_assumption: Preserving the remaining schedule structure is preferred to short-term mileage compensation.

rules.summary: Use phase-appropriate recipes with explicit quality-work progression, recovery, specificity, and taper decisions.
rules.product_assumption: Exact work-distance increments, repetition formats, and recovery durations are transparent deterministic construction choices; the cited evidence does not establish one universal prescription.

rules.summary: Progress climbing, controlled descending, and race-like terrain while prescribing trail work by effort.
rules.product_assumption: Exact ascent fractions, progression limits, technicality labels, and the 1500-metre supported-course boundary are deterministic product choices rather than universal physiological thresholds.
